subject: Electrical Engineering
title: ALU: The Calculator Inside the Processor
description: A micro-lesson that makes ALU: The Calculator Inside the Processor usable.

hook.text: The ALU — Arithmetic Logic Unit — does the math and logic inside every CPU.

buildup.text: It combines adders, shifters, and logic gates. Control signals select the operation.

discovery.text: One ALU can add, subtract, AND, OR, XOR, shift, and compare — all with the same hardware.

twist.text: Modern CPUs have multiple ALUs working in parallel — executing several operations per clock cycle.

climax.text: GPUs contain thousands of simple ALUs — perfect for parallel math in graphics and AI.

punchline.text: Add, compare, shift — the ALU does math one operation at a time.

quiz.question: What distinguishes a GPU from a CPU in terms of ALUs?
options: GPUs have one very fast ALU; CPUs have many slow ones
GPUs contain thousands of simple ALUs for massive parallelism
GPUs don't use ALUs — they use dedicated graphics hardware
